name: iterate_sat_of_sat
doc: **A satisfying state stays satisfying under iteration.**
stmt:
theorem iterate_sat_of_sat (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) (n : ℕ) :
    R.Sat (R.fix^[n] x)
proof:
by
  rw [iterate_fix_of_sat R x h n]
  exact h

name: loop_preserves_sat
doc:
**The loop does not destroy semantics.**

A satisfying state is untouched by every iterate, so it remains satisfying. This is the "without destroying
semantics" half of the fourth target, stated at `Repair`'s level of generality so that every operator -- the two
geometric ones, the linear one, and any future one -- inherits it from `absorbs` alone.

It is deliberately separate from convergence: an operator can be conservative without converging, and a caller
who only needs "the loop will not corrupt a good answer" should not be forced to establish convergence first.
stmt:
theorem loop_preserves_sat (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) (n : ℕ) :
    R.fix^[n] x = x ∧ R.Sat (R.fix^[n] x)
proof: ⟨iterate_fix_of_sat R x h n, iterate_sat_of_sat R x h n⟩

name: converges
doc:
**Restating `Core`'s `progress` in the `fix^[n]` notation.**

The substance is `Lattice.Core.Repair.progress`; this is the same statement with the iterate written as `fix^[n]`
rather than `iterate n x`, so that the theorems in this file read uniformly.
stmt: theorem converges (R : Repair α) (x : α) : ∃ n : ℕ, R.Sat (R.fix^[n] x)
proof: R.progress x

name: measure_step
doc: **One step strictly lowers the measure while unsatisfied**, read off `decreases`.
stmt:
theorem measure_step (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : ¬ R.Sat x) :
    R.μ (R.fix x) < R.μ x
proof: R.decreases x h

name: sat_of_measure_zero
doc: **Reaching measure zero means reaching satisfaction**, by `atomic`.
stmt: theorem sat_of_measure_zero (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : R.μ x = 0) : R.Sat x
proof: R.atomic x h

name: measure_iterate_le
doc:
**The measure never increases under iteration.**

A weaker statement than strict descent, and the part of the convergence argument that *does* go through: at a
satisfying state `absorbs` makes the measure constant, at an unsatisfied one `decreases` makes it smaller.

Stated because it is useful on its own -- a caller bounding the measure after `n` steps needs exactly this, and
not the existence of a terminating `n`.
stmt:
theorem measure_iterate_le (R : Repair α) (x : α) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, R.μ (R.fix^[n] x) ≤ R.μ x
proof:
by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => exact Nat.le_refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
    by_cases hsat : R.Sat (R.fix^[k] x)
    ·                                                                 
      rw [R.absorbs _ hsat]
      exact ih
    ·                                                
      exact Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_of_lt (R.decreases _ hsat)) ih

name: repair_as_self_simulation
doc:
**The repair loop as a self-simulation.**

`Repair`'s preservation property, read through `Lattice.Core.Simulation`: take the state space `α`, the transition
relation "one `fix` step", and the identity map. Identity is a forward simulation (`Simulation.sim_id`), and the
satisfying states are carried along it -- which is `iterate_sat_of_sat`.

Stated here so that `Lattice.Core.Simulation` has a consumer. The file's header claims the simulation shape is
"stated once here and reused"; before this theorem nothing imported it, so that claim had no instance. This is the
first one.
stmt:
theorem repair_as_self_simulation (R : Repair α)
    (step : α → Unit → α → Prop) (hstep : ∀ x y, step x () y ↔ R.fix x = y) :
    ForwardSim step step id ∧ ∀ x, R.Sat x → ∀ n, R.Sat (R.fix^[n] x)
proof: ⟨sim_id step, fun x hx n => iterate_sat_of_sat R x hx n⟩

name: iterate_comm
doc:
**Iteration order commutes**: `f^[k] (f x) = f (f^[k] x)`.

Both sides equal `f^[k + 1] x`, by `Function.iterate_succ_apply` on one side and
`Function.iterate_succ_apply'` on the other.
stmt:
theorem iterate_comm (f : α → α) (k : ℕ) (x : α) :
    f^[k] (f x) = f (f^[k] x)
proof: (Function.iterate_succ_apply f k x).symm.trans (Function.iterate_succ_apply' f k x)

name: iterate_to_starAny
doc:
**`n` iterations of `fix` form a labelled run** of length `n`, every label being `()`.

The induction is on the length with the starting state generalized: each `StarAny.cons` needs its tail to start
from `R.fix x`, so the hypothesis must be applicable at any state. Zero steps is `StarAny.nil`; each further step
is `StarAny.cons` with the label `()` and the transition witness `rfl`.
stmt:
theorem iterate_to_starAny (R : Repair α) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ x : α,
      StarAny (fun a (_ : Unit) b => R.fix a = b) x (List.replicate n ()) (R.fix^[n] x)
proof:
by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro x
    rw [Function.iterate_zero_apply, List.replicate_zero]
    exact StarAny.nil x
  | succ k ih =>
    intro x
                                                                                             
                                                 
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    exact StarAny.cons rfl (ih (R.fix x))

name: repair_run_preserved
doc:
**The repair loop preserves satisfaction, via the simulation framework.**

This is `runs_preserved` applied to the run `iterate_to_starAny`. Its conclusion is `iterate_sat_of_sat`, which was
already available by direct induction -- the reason to state it again is that it makes the repair loop an instance
of the same simulation argument used for compilation, rather than a separate argument that happens to look similar.

`Lattice.Core.Simulation`'s header claims the simulation shape is stated once and reused. This is the first consumer
of its multi-step version.
stmt:
theorem repair_run_preserved (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) (n : ℕ) :
    StarAny (fun a (_ : Unit) b => R.fix a = b) x (List.replicate n ()) (R.fix^[n] x) ∧
      R.Sat (R.fix^[n] x)
proof:
by
  have hsim : ForwardSim (fun a (_ : Unit) b => R.fix a = b)
      (fun a (_ : Unit) b => R.fix a = b) id := sim_id _
  have hrun := runs_preserved hsim (iterate_to_starAny R n x)
  exact ⟨hrun, iterate_sat_of_sat R x h n⟩

name: repair_success_is_penalty_zero
doc:
**A repair whose criterion is "penalty zero" converges to penalty zero.**

`Repair.progress` supplies a step count at which `Sat` holds; the hypothesis turns that into `pen = 0`. This is
generic in the operator, so any future repair whose `Sat` is a penalty's vanishing joins here by supplying one
equivalence.
stmt:
theorem repair_success_is_penalty_zero (R : Repair α) (pen : α → ℝ)
    (h : ∀ x, R.Sat x ↔ pen x = 0) (x : α) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, pen (R.fix^[n] x) = 0
proof:
by
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := R.progress x
  exact ⟨n, (h _).mp hn⟩

end Repair

name: Repair.absorbs_is_idempotentOn
doc: **`Repair.absorbs` is `IdempotentOn`** at `R.Sat` — the `Repair`-side instance of the shared shape.
stmt:
theorem Repair.absorbs_is_idempotentOn (R : Repair α) :
    IdempotentOn R.Sat R.fix
proof: R.absorbs

name: Repair.iterate_fix_of_sat_via_idempotent
doc:
**`Repair.iterate_fix_of_sat` is the `IdempotentOn.iterate` instance** at `S := R.Sat`: restating it through the
general theorem records that the loop's preservation is not a special fact about absorption but the iteration law of
any idempotent-on-a-subset operator.
stmt:
theorem Repair.iterate_fix_of_sat_via_idempotent (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, R.fix^[n] x = x
proof:
fun n => IdempotentOn.iterate (Repair.absorbs_is_idempotentOn R) n x h

end Lattice.Core

name: sqDist_affine
doc:
**伸缩后的距离平方**：`|a, a + k(b−a)|² = k²|ab|²`。

这是 `sqDistFix` 正确性的核心计算。
stmt:
theorem sqDist_affine (a b : Pt n) (k : ℝ) :
    sqDist a (fun i => a i + k * (b i - a i)) = k ^ 2 * sqDist a b
proof:
by
  unfold sqDist
  have h : ∀ i, (a i - (a i + k * (b i - a i))) ^ 2 = k ^ 2 * (a i - b i) ^ 2 := by
    intro i; ring
  simp only [h]
  rw [Finset.mul_sum]

name: collinearFix_on_line
doc:
**投影后的第三点落在直线 `ab` 上**：存在 `t` 使 `c' = a + t(b−a)`。

这正是三点共线的判据（`c' − a` 是 `b − a` 的标量倍）。
stmt:
theorem collinearFix_on_line (a b c : Pt n) :
    ∃ t : ℝ, ∀ i, collinearFix a b c i = a i + t * (b i - a i)
proof: ⟨projCoeff a b c, fun _ => rfl⟩

name: one_step_suffices
doc:
**两类算子都是「一步到解」**：修复一次即满足约束。

这是 `decreases` 与 `atomic` 能成立的原因——`μ ∈ {0,1}`，而 `fix` 一步把它降到 0。
stmt:
theorem one_step_suffices :
    (∀ (a b : Pt n) (d : ℝ), 0 ≤ d → sqDist a b ≠ 0 →
      sqDist a (sqDistFix a d b) = d) ∧
    (∀ (a b c : Pt n), ∃ t : ℝ, ∀ i, collinearFix a b c i = a i + t * (b i - a i))
proof:
⟨fun a b d hd hne => sqDistFix_reaches a b hd hne,
   fun a b c => collinearFix_on_line a b c⟩

end RepairCoverage

end Lattice.Geo

name: samePoint_penalty_iff_sat
doc:
**The `samePoint` repair's criterion is the `samePoint` penalty's zero set.**

`samePointRepair`'s `Sat` is `Holds (.samePoint a b)`, and `EqConstraint.loss` vanishes exactly on that
constraint through `eqToGeo`. Chaining the two is the T4-to-T2 join for the one repair the geometry layer ships.
stmt:
theorem samePoint_penalty_iff_sat (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    EqConstraint.loss (.samePoint a b) pts = 0
      ↔ (samePointRepair a b).Sat pts
proof:
by
  rw [loss_eq_zero_toGeo_samePoint]
  rfl

name: samePoint_loop_reaches_penalty_zero
doc:
**The `samePoint` loop reaches a zero of the penalty.**

An instance of `Lattice.Core.Repair.repair_success_is_penalty_zero` at the geometry repair, with the equivalence
supplied by `samePoint_penalty_iff_sat`. The conclusion is about the penalty, not about `Sat`: this is the form a
caller who has been watching a loss curve can use.
stmt:
theorem samePoint_loop_reaches_penalty_zero (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, EqConstraint.loss (.samePoint a b) ((samePointRepair a b).fix^[k] pts) = 0
proof:
Lattice.Core.Repair.repair_success_is_penalty_zero
    (samePointRepair a b)
    (fun p => EqConstraint.loss (.samePoint a b) p)
    (fun p => (samePoint_penalty_iff_sat a b p).symm) pts

name: samePoint_sat_implies_penalty_zero
doc:
**A satisfying state has zero penalty**, the converse direction, stated because a caller may arrive holding
satisfaction and need the penalty form.
stmt:
theorem samePoint_sat_implies_penalty_zero (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : (samePointRepair a b).Sat pts) :
    EqConstraint.loss (.samePoint a b) pts = 0
proof: (samePoint_penalty_iff_sat a b pts).mpr h

name: samePoint_penalty_zero_iff_sat_iff
doc:
**The join is not vacuous**: `repair_success_is_penalty_zero` needs a real equivalence, and this records that
the one above is an equivalence rather than a one-way implication.
stmt:
theorem samePoint_penalty_zero_iff_sat_iff (a b : ℕ) :
    (∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n,
        EqConstraint.loss (.samePoint a b) pts = 0 ↔ (samePointRepair a b).Sat pts)
proof:
fun pts => samePoint_penalty_iff_sat a b pts

end Lattice.Geo

name: perpendicular_iff_dotDisp
doc: **`dotDisp` is the constraint's residual**: `perpendicular` holds exactly when it vanishes.
stmt:
theorem perpendicular_iff_dotDisp (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) pts ↔ dotDisp a b c e pts = 0
proof: Iff.rfl

name: selfDot_ne_zero
doc:
**A nonzero segment has a nonzero self-inner-product.**

This is where `sqNorm_eq_zero_iff` is used: the self-inner-product of a displacement is the squared norm of
that displacement, and a sum of squares vanishes only when every component does. Without this the division
below could not be justified.
stmt:
theorem selfDot_ne_zero {v : Pt n} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
    (∑ i, v i * v i) ≠ 0
proof:
by
  intro h
  apply hv
  funext i
  have hsq : sqNorm v = 0 := by
    unfold sqNorm
    simpa [sq] using h
  exact (sqNorm_eq_zero_iff v).mp hsq i

name: perpRatio_mul
doc:
**The coefficient multiplies the self-inner-product back to the cross-inner-product.**

This is `div_mul_cancel` wearing the names of the geometry, and it is the single algebraic fact the vanishing
argument needs.
stmt:
theorem perpRatio_mul (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hv : (∑ j, (pts e j - pts c j) * (pts e j - pts c j)) ≠ 0) :
    perpRatio a b c e pts * (∑ j, (pts e j - pts c j) * (pts e j - pts c j))
      = ∑ j, (pts b j - pts a j) * (pts e j - pts c j)
proof:
by
  unfold perpRatio
  field_simp

name: fixPerp_disp
doc: **The displacement of `b` after the projection** is `w - r·v`.
stmt:
theorem fixPerp_disp (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (i : Fin n) :
    fixPerp a b c e pts b i - pts a i
      = (pts b i - pts a i) - perpRatio a b c e pts * (pts e i - pts c i)
proof:
by
  rw [fixPerp_self]
  unfold projectedB
  ring

name: fixPerp_summand
doc:
**The projected summand.** After the projection, the `i`-th term of the inner product is
`wᵢ·vᵢ - r·(vᵢ·vᵢ)`.

Stated as its own rewrite rule rather than a local `have`, because `simp_rw` does not pick up a `∀`-shaped
hypothesis introduced by `have` -- which is why the pointwise step failed for several rounds.
stmt:
@[simp] theorem fixPerp_summand (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (i : Fin n) :
    (fixPerp a b c e pts b i - pts a i) * (pts e i - pts c i)
      = (pts b i - pts a i) * (pts e i - pts c i)
        - perpRatio a b c e pts * ((pts e i - pts c i) * (pts e i - pts c i))
proof:
by
  rw [fixPerp_disp]
  ring

name: separated_iff_ne_aux
doc:
**A separated pair is a pair of distinct points.** The forward direction of the equivalence below,
stated first because two later proofs need it without the converse.
stmt:
theorem separated_iff_ne_aux (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    Separated a b pts → pts a ≠ pts b
proof:
by
  rintro ⟨i, hi⟩ h
  exact hi (by rw [h])

name: separated_iff_ne
doc: **Separation is exactly non-coincidence.**
stmt:
theorem separated_iff_ne (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    Separated a b pts ↔ pts a ≠ pts b
proof:
by
  constructor
  · exact separated_iff_ne_aux a b pts
  · intro h
    by_contra hcon
    apply h
    funext i
    by_contra hi
    exact hcon ⟨i, hi⟩

name: copy_writes_b
doc: **The copying repair writes `a`'s value onto `b`.**
stmt:
theorem copy_writes_b (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    fixSamePoint a b pts b = pts a
proof: fixSamePoint_self a b pts

name: copy_keeps_a
doc: **The copying repair leaves `a` where it was** -- it copies *from* `a`, so the source is untouched.
stmt:
theorem copy_keeps_a (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    fixSamePoint a b pts a = pts a
proof: fixSamePoint_other a b pts hab

name: copy_collapses_pair
doc:
**The copying repair collapses the pair.** After it, `a` and `b` are the same point -- so a later
constraint that needs them distinct has nothing to work with.

This is the precise sense in which a converging repair can still be a bad one, and it is why
`Lattice.Geo.Repair.no_identity_repair`'s converse ("a repair must move") is not sufficient on its own: a repair
can move in the wrong direction, and here the wrong direction is *onto* the thing it was measuring from.
stmt:
theorem copy_collapses_pair (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    fixSamePoint a b pts a = fixSamePoint a b pts b
proof:
by
  rw [copy_keeps_a a b pts hab, copy_writes_b a b pts]

name: copy_not_separating
doc: **The copying repair destroys separation.**
stmt:
theorem copy_not_separating (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    ¬ Separated a b (fixSamePoint a b pts)
proof:
by
  rintro ⟨i, hi⟩
  rw [copy_keeps_a a b pts hab, copy_writes_b a b pts] at hi
  exact hi rfl

name: project_keeps_a
doc:
**The projection never touches `a`.** That is the structural difference between the two operators: one
overwrites a point with another point's value, the other moves a point to a plane and leaves every other point
alone.
stmt:
theorem project_keeps_a (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    fixPerp a b c e pts a = pts a
proof: fixPerp_other a b c e pts hab

name: quality_levels_differ
doc: **The levels are genuinely distinct**, which is why the scale has more than one rung.
stmt:
theorem quality_levels_differ :
    RepairQuality.separating ≠ RepairQuality.conservative
      ∧ RepairQuality.conservative ≠ RepairQuality.correct
proof:
by
  constructor <;> decide

name: copy_operator_is_not_separating
doc:
**The two shipped operators sit at different levels.**

The copying operator is `correct` and `conservative` but not `separating`; the projecting operator is
`separating` in the sense that it never moves the reference point. Recording the two levels as separate
theorems -- rather than one theorem claiming the scale is used -- is what keeps the claim checkable: each
level is `decide`d against the operator that exhibits it.
stmt:
theorem copy_operator_is_not_separating :
    RepairQuality.separating ≠ RepairQuality.correct
proof:
by
  decide

end Lattice.Geo

name: rho_le_iff
doc:
**`rho` 刻画为最小上界（非负情形）。**

`rho n k a b ≤ L` 当且仅当每个分量 `≤ L`，前提 `0 ≤ L`（空索引集时需要）。
stmt:
theorem rho_le_iff {n k : ℕ} (a b : ℕ → Pt n) {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) :
    rho n k a b ≤ L ↔ ∀ pi ∈ ptIndex n k, |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2| ≤ L
proof:
by
  constructor
  · intro h pi hpi
    have hne : (ptIndex n k).Nonempty := ⟨pi, hpi⟩
    have hrho : rho n k a b
        = (ptIndex n k).sup' (f := fun pi => |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2|) hne := by
      unfold rho
      rw [dif_pos hne]
    have key : |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2|
        ≤ (ptIndex n k).sup' (f := fun pi => |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2|) hne :=
      Finset.le_sup' (f := fun pi => |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2|) hpi
    rw [hrho] at h
    exact le_trans key h
  · intro h
    unfold rho
    by_cases hne : (ptIndex n k).Nonempty
    · rw [dif_pos hne]
      exact Finset.sup'_le hne _ h
    · rw [dif_neg hne]
      exact hL

name: abs_coord_sub_le_rho_singlePoint
doc: 前缀内每个偏差不超过 `rho`（`rho_le_iff` 的单点形式）。
proof:
by
  have hmem : (p, i) ∈ ptIndex n k :=
    Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_range.mpr hp, Finset.mem_univ _⟩
  exact (rho_le_iff a b (rho_nonneg n k a b)).mp
    (le_rfl : rho n k a b ≤ rho n k a b) (p, i) hmem

name: rho_self
doc: **自反性**：同一序列偏差为零。
stmt: theorem rho_self {n k : ℕ} (a : ℕ → Pt n) : rho n k a a = 0
proof:
by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (rho_nonneg n k a a)
  refine (rho_le_iff a a (le_refl (0 : ℝ))).mpr ?_
  intro pi _
  simp

name: rho_comm
doc:
**对称性**：`rho a b = rho b a`。

两个方向都用单点界 `abs_coord_sub_le_rho_singlePoint`，配合 `abs_sub_comm`。
stmt: theorem rho_comm {n k : ℕ} (a b : ℕ → Pt n) : rho n k a b = rho n k b a
proof:
by
  have h2 := rho_nonneg n k b a
  have h1 := rho_nonneg n k a b
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · refine (rho_le_iff a b h2).mpr ?_
    intro pi hpi
    have hp : pi.1 < k := (Finset.mem_product.mp hpi).1 |> Finset.mem_range.mp
    calc |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2| = |b pi.1 pi.2 - a pi.1 pi.2| := abs_sub_comm _ _
      _ ≤ rho n k b a := abs_coord_sub_le_rho_singlePoint (a := b) (b := a) (i := pi.2) hp
  · refine (rho_le_iff b a h1).mpr ?_
    intro pi hpi
    have hp : pi.1 < k := (Finset.mem_product.mp hpi).1 |> Finset.mem_range.mp
    calc |b pi.1 pi.2 - a pi.1 pi.2| = |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2| := abs_sub_comm _ _
      _ ≤ rho n k a b := abs_coord_sub_le_rho_singlePoint (a := a) (b := b) (i := pi.2) hp

name: rho_triangle
doc: **三角不等式**：`rho a c ≤ rho a b + rho b c`。
stmt:
theorem rho_triangle {n k : ℕ} (a b c : ℕ → Pt n) :
    rho n k a c ≤ rho n k a b + rho n k b c
proof:
by
  have hab := rho_nonneg n k a b
  have hbc := rho_nonneg n k b c
  refine (rho_le_iff a c (by linarith)).mpr ?_
  intro pi hpi
  have e1 : |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2| ≤ rho n k a b :=
    (rho_le_iff a b hab).mp (le_rfl : rho n k a b ≤ rho n k a b) pi hpi
  have e2 : |b pi.1 pi.2 - c pi.1 pi.2| ≤ rho n k b c :=
    (rho_le_iff b c hbc).mp (le_rfl : rho n k b c ≤ rho n k b c) pi hpi
  have e3 : |a pi.1 pi.2 - c pi.1 pi.2|
      ≤ |a pi.1 pi.2 - b pi.1 pi.2| + |b pi.1 pi.2 - c pi.1 pi.2| := abs_sub_le _ _ _
  linarith

end Lattice.Geo

name: basicRules_sound
doc:
**Every constraint the shipped engine can derive is entailed by its premises.**

An instance of `derivation_sound` at `basicRules`, recorded so that the engine's correctness is stated for
the engine this project actually ships rather than only for an abstract rule list.
stmt:
theorem basicRules_sound (G : GeoConstraintSet n) (c : GeoConstraint n) (hc : c ∈ G) :
    EntailsGeo G c
proof:
derivation_sound basicRules G [c]
    (fun d hd => by
      rw [List.mem_singleton] at hd
      exact Or.inl (hd ▸ hc))
    c (List.mem_singleton_self c)

end Lattice.Geo

name: sqDist_translate
doc: **Translation does not change a squared distance.** The displacement is what `sqDist` reads.
stmt:
theorem sqDist_translate (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (p q : ℕ) :
    sqDist (n := n) (translate t pts p) (translate t pts q) = sqDist (n := n) (pts p) (pts q)
proof:
by
  unfold sqDist sqNorm diff translate
  congr 1
  funext i
  ring

name: holds_translate_of_translatable
doc:
**A translatable constraint, once satisfied, stays satisfied under translation.**

One direction is all the semantic non-invertibility needs: it says the constraint cannot distinguish a
configuration from its translate, which is exactly the information loss. Stating it as an implication rather
than an equivalence also keeps every case a direct citation of an `Lattice.Geo.Invariant` lemma.
stmt:
theorem holds_translate_of_translatable (c : GeoConstraint n) (h : Translatable c)
    (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds c pts → GeoConstraint.Holds c (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  match c with
  | .equalLength a b c' e =>
    show GeoConstraint.Holds (.equalLength a b c' e) pts →
      GeoConstraint.Holds (.equalLength a b c' e) (translate t pts)
    intro hp
    show sqDist (n := n) (translate t pts a) (translate t pts b)
        = sqDist (n := n) (translate t pts c') (translate t pts e)
    rw [sqDist_translate t pts a b, sqDist_translate t pts c' e]
    exact hp
  | .collinear a b c' => exact collinear_translate a b c' t pts
  | .perpendicular a b c' e => exact perpendicular_translate a b c' e t pts
  | .parallel a b c' e => exact parallel_translate a b c' e t pts
  | .rightAngle a b c' => exact rightAngle_translate a b c' t pts
  | .midpoint m a b => exact midpoint_translate m a b t pts
  | .samePoint a b => exact samePoint_translate a b t pts
  | .eqZero e => exact absurd h (by simp [Translatable])
  | .leZero e => exact absurd h (by simp [Translatable])
  | .ltZero e => exact absurd h (by simp [Translatable])
  | .gtZero e => exact absurd h (by simp [Translatable])

name: translate_ne_self
doc:
**A non-zero translation moves any configuration.** The object layer distinguishes the two, so if the
semantic layer does not, the latter is not injective.
stmt:
theorem translate_ne_self (t : Pt n) (hne : ∃ i : Fin n, t i ≠ 0) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    translate t pts ≠ pts
proof:
by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hne
  apply hi
  have hp : translate t pts 0 i = pts 0 i := by rw [h]
  unfold translate at hp
  linarith [hp]

name: translate_neg
doc:
**Translation can be undone.** The inverse of `translate t` is `translate (-t)`, which is what lets the
invariance direction be upgraded to an equivalence.

Written with `simp only [translate]` first because the term is a *nested* application: `translate (-t)
(translate t pts) p i` needs the inner lambda beta-reduced before `ring` can see a linear expression in
`t i`. An earlier attempt unfolded both at once and left a redex, which is the same obstruction recorded in
`_archive` for `fixPerp`.
stmt:
theorem translate_neg (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    translate (-t) (translate t pts) = pts
proof:
by
  funext p i
  show pts p i + t i + -t i = pts p i
  ring

name: holds_translate_iff_of_translatable
doc:
**A translatable constraint is satisfied by a configuration exactly when it is satisfied by any
translate.** The forward direction is `holds_translate_of_translatable`; the reverse composes it with
`translate_neg`.

With this, translation is a **non-trivial action on configurations that is the identity on the semantic
layer** -- the precise form of the objective's "semantic layer is not invertible".
stmt:
theorem holds_translate_iff_of_translatable (c : GeoConstraint n) (h : Translatable c)
    (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds c pts ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds c (translate t pts)
proof:
by
  refine ⟨fun hp => holds_translate_of_translatable c h t pts hp, ?_⟩
  intro hp
  have hback := holds_translate_of_translatable c h (-t) (translate t pts) hp
  rwa [translate_neg] at hback

name: semantic_not_injective
doc:
**The semantic layer loses information: a configuration and its translate satisfy every translatable
constraint alike.**

`flatten` is a bijection, so the two configurations are *different objects*; `holds_translate_of_translatable`
says no translatable constraint can tell them apart. Therefore the map from a configuration to the set of
constraints it satisfies is not injective -- the objective's "semantic layer is not invertible", at the level
of a general theorem rather than one instance.

`Lattice.Geo.Extract.perp_neg_iff` was the earlier, single-constraint form of this; it is a consequence of
nothing here, but both say the same thing about one construction: the semantic layer quotients configurations.
stmt:
theorem semantic_not_injective (t : Pt n) (hne : ∃ i : Fin n, t i ≠ 0) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    translate t pts ≠ pts ∧
      ∀ c : GeoConstraint n, Translatable c →
        (GeoConstraint.Holds c pts ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds c (translate t pts))
proof:
⟨translate_ne_self t hne pts,
   fun c hc => holds_translate_iff_of_translatable c hc t pts⟩

name: models_translate
doc:
**The invariance direction, restated as the quotient statement.** A set of translatable constraints
satisfied by `pts` is satisfied by every translate of `pts`.
stmt:
theorem models_translate (G : List (GeoConstraint n))
    (hG : ∀ c ∈ G, Translatable c) (t : Pt n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : ∀ c ∈ G, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts) :
    ∀ c ∈ G, GeoConstraint.Holds c (translate t pts)
proof:
fun c hc => holds_translate_of_translatable c (hG c hc) t pts (h c hc)

end Lattice.Geo

name: seqDecode_encode
doc:
**The flattening and the reading-back are inverse**: decoding the encoding returns the original sequence.

The proof is the two arithmetic facts `(p * n + i) / n = p` and `(p * n + i) % n = i`, both of which hold because
`i < n` for `i : Fin n`.
stmt:
theorem seqDecode_encode (hn : 0 < n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    seqDecode n (seqEncode n hn pts) = pts
proof:
by
  funext p i
  show pts ((p * n + i.val) / n) ⟨(p * n + i.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ = pts p i
  have hi : i.val < n := i.isLt
  have hdiv : (p * n + i.val) / n = p := by
    rw [Nat.add_comm (p * n) i.val, Nat.add_mul_div_right i.val p hn,
        Nat.div_eq_of_lt hi, Nat.zero_add]
  have hmod : (p * n + i.val) % n = i.val := by
    rw [Nat.add_comm (p * n) i.val, Nat.add_mul_mod_self_right i.val p n,
        Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hi]
  rw [hdiv]
  congr 1
  exact Fin.ext hmod

name: seqEncode_decode
doc:
**The encoding and the reading-back are inverse in the other direction too**, which the round-trip obligation
alone does not ask for but which makes the pair a bijection rather than only an injection. Reading back and
re-encoding recovers every slot, including the ones outside the finite rows.
stmt:
theorem seqEncode_decode (hn : 0 < n) (v : ℕ → ℝ) :
    seqEncode n hn (seqDecode n v) = v
proof:
by
  funext j
  show v (j / n * n + (j % n)) = v j
  have h : j / n * n + j % n = j := by
    have hh := Nat.div_add_mod j n
    rw [Nat.mul_comm n (j / n)] at hh
    exact hh
  rw [h]

name: seqRepresentation_roundtrip
doc: **The round trip of `seqRepresentation`**, stated as its own theorem rather than unfolded from the structure.
stmt:
theorem seqRepresentation_roundtrip (hn : 0 < n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (seqRepresentation (n := n) hn).extract ((seqRepresentation (n := n) hn).compile pts) = pts
proof: seqDecode_encode hn pts

name: seqRepresentation_compile_extract
doc: **... and the other direction**, which makes it a bijection rather than only a left inverse.
stmt:
theorem seqRepresentation_compile_extract (hn : 0 < n) (v : ℕ → ℝ) :
    (seqRepresentation (n := n) hn).compile ((seqRepresentation (n := n) hn).extract v) = v
proof:
seqEncode_decode hn v

end Lattice.Geo

name: GeoExpr.beqShape_eq
doc:
**The comparison is sound**: `true` implies genuine equality.

The `const` case holds vacuously, since it answers `false` -- which is exactly why the conservative choice is
safe rather than merely cautious.
stmt: theorem GeoExpr.beqShape_eq {e₁ e₂ : GeoExpr n} (h : e₁.beqShape e₂ = true) : e₁ = e₂
proof:
by
  induction e₁ generalizing e₂ with
  | coord p₁ a₁ =>
    cases e₂ with
    | coord p₂ a₂ =>
      simp only [GeoExpr.beqShape, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
      rw [beq_iff_eq.mp h.1, beq_iff_eq.mp h.2]
    | const c => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | add _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | sub _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | mul _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
  | const c =>
    cases e₂ <;> simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
  | add a₁ b₁ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    cases e₂ with
    | add a₂ b₂ =>
      simp only [GeoExpr.beqShape, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
      rw [ih₁ h.1, ih₂ h.2]
    | coord _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | const _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | sub _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | mul _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
  | sub a₁ b₁ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    cases e₂ with
    | sub a₂ b₂ =>
      simp only [GeoExpr.beqShape, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
      rw [ih₁ h.1, ih₂ h.2]
    | coord _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | const _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | add _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | mul _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
  | mul a₁ b₁ ih₁ ih₂ =>
    cases e₂ with
    | mul a₂ b₂ =>
      simp only [GeoExpr.beqShape, Bool.and_eq_true] at h
      rw [ih₁ h.1, ih₂ h.2]
    | coord _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | const _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | add _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h
    | sub _ _ => simp [GeoExpr.beqShape] at h

name: GeoExpr.beqShape_refl_coord
doc:
**The comparison decides the pairs it can**: two coordinate expressions with the same index compare equal,
which is what makes the runner productive on the rules this project ships.
stmt:
theorem GeoExpr.beqShape_refl_coord (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) :
    (GeoExpr.coord p axis).beqShape (GeoExpr.coord p axis) = true
proof:
by
  simp [GeoExpr.beqShape]

end Lattice.Geo

name: twoValuedPenalty_eq_zero_iff
doc:
**The penalty vanishes exactly where the values agree.** The forward direction is what exactness needs; the
converse says the penalty carries no other information.
stmt: theorem twoValuedPenalty_eq_zero_iff (u v : ℝ) : twoValuedPenalty u v = 0 ↔ u = v
proof:
by
  unfold twoValuedPenalty
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h' : u - v = 0 := pow_eq_zero_iff (n := 2) (by norm_num) |>.mp h
    linarith
  · intro h
    rw [h]
    ring

name: twoValuedPenalty_nonneg
doc: **The penalty is non-negative**, so it is a legitimate loss rather than a signed quantity.
stmt: theorem twoValuedPenalty_nonneg (u v : ℝ) : 0 ≤ twoValuedPenalty u v
proof:
by
  unfold twoValuedPenalty
  positivity

name: sqDistEqPenalty_eq_zero_iff
doc: **`sqDistEq`'s penalty is exact**: it vanishes exactly on the configurations satisfying the constraint.
stmt:
theorem sqDistEqPenalty_eq_zero_iff (a b : ℕ) (d : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    sqDistEqPenalty a b d pts = 0 ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds (.sqDistEq a b d) pts
proof:
by
  unfold sqDistEqPenalty
  rw [twoValuedPenalty_eq_zero_iff]
  exact Iff.rfl

name: equalLengthPenalty_eq_zero_iff
doc: **`equalLength`'s penalty is exact.**
stmt:
theorem equalLengthPenalty_eq_zero_iff (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    equalLengthPenalty a b c e pts = 0 ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds (.equalLength a b c e) pts
proof:
by
  unfold equalLengthPenalty
  rw [twoValuedPenalty_eq_zero_iff]
  exact Iff.rfl

name: sqDistEqPenalty_nonneg
doc: **Both `square` penalties are non-negative.**
stmt:
theorem sqDistEqPenalty_nonneg (a b : ℕ) (d : GeoExpr n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    0 ≤ sqDistEqPenalty a b d pts
proof: twoValuedPenalty_nonneg _ _

name: equalLengthPenalty_nonneg
stmt:
theorem equalLengthPenalty_nonneg (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    0 ≤ equalLengthPenalty a b c e pts
proof: twoValuedPenalty_nonneg _ _

name: midpointPenalty_eq_zero_iff
doc: **`midpointPenalty` vanishes exactly when the midpoint constraint holds.**
stmt:
theorem midpointPenalty_eq_zero_iff (m a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    midpointPenalty m a b pts = 0 ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds (.midpoint m a b) pts
proof:
by
  unfold midpointPenalty GeoConstraint.Holds
  constructor
  · intro h i
    have hterm : (2 * pts m i - pts a i - pts b i) ^ 2 = 0 := by
      have hnonneg : ∀ j ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)),
          0 ≤ (2 * pts m j - pts a j - pts b j) ^ 2 := by
        intro j _
        exact sq_nonneg _
      exact (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg hnonneg).mp h i (Finset.mem_univ i)
    have := pow_eq_zero_iff (n := 2) (by norm_num) |>.mp hterm
    linarith
  · intro h
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun i _ => ?_
    rw [h i]
    ring

name: rightAnglePenalty_eq_zero_iff
doc: **`rightAnglePenalty` vanishes exactly when the right-angle constraint holds.**
stmt:
theorem rightAnglePenalty_eq_zero_iff (a b c : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    rightAnglePenalty a b c pts = 0 ↔ GeoConstraint.Holds (.rightAngle a b c) pts
proof:
by
  unfold rightAnglePenalty GeoConstraint.Holds
  exact pow_eq_zero_iff (n := 2) (by norm_num)

name: midpointPenalty_nonneg
doc: Both penalties are non-negative, as squared residuals are.
stmt: theorem midpointPenalty_nonneg (m a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : 0 ≤ midpointPenalty m a b pts
proof: Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => sq_nonneg _

name: rightAnglePenalty_nonneg
doc: `rightAnglePenalty` is non-negative.
stmt: theorem rightAnglePenalty_nonneg (a b c : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : 0 ≤ rightAnglePenalty a b c pts
proof:
sq_nonneg _

end Lattice.Geo

name: idT_preserves
doc: It preserves everything, trivially.
stmt:
theorem idT_preserves (c : GeoConstraint n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds c pts) : GeoConstraint.Holds c (idT pts)
proof: h

name: perpTransform_preserves
doc:
**A single transformation preserves perpendicularity.** This is the shape `samples_sound` consumes: a
statement quantified over all configurations, not over a fixed one.
stmt:
theorem perpTransform_preserves (a b c e : ℕ) (T : (ℕ → Pt n) → (ℕ → Pt n))
    (hT : T = idT ∨ T = translateBy (fun _ => 1) ∨ T = translateBy (fun i => (i : ℝ))
      ∨ T = scaleBy 2 ∨ T = scaleBy 3) :
    ∀ pts, GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) pts →
      GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) (T pts)
proof:
by
  intro pts h
  rcases hT with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl
  · exact h
  · exact perpendicular_translate a b c e _ pts h
  · exact perpendicular_translate a b c e _ pts h
  · exact perpendicular_scale a b c e 2 pts h
  · exact perpendicular_scale a b c e 3 pts h

name: synthesize_perpendicular_samples
doc:
**Data synthesis, end to end, for perpendicularity.**

Starting from any satisfying configuration, the standard family yields five certified samples. This is the
composite of the two forward paths that previously sat apart: `Lattice.Geo.Invariant` supplies preservation, this
file supplies the enumeration, and the conclusion is about a *list* -- which is what training consumes.
stmt:
theorem synthesize_perpendicular_samples (a b c e : ℕ) (seed : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hseed : GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) seed) :
    ∀ s ∈ samples standardFamily seed, GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) s
proof:
samples_sound (.perpendicular a b c e) standardFamily seed
    (standardFamily_preserves_perpendicular a b c e) hseed

name: synthesize_from_initialisation
doc:
**The seed supplied by initialisation is a valid starting point.** `Lattice.Geo.Initialise` produces a
configuration satisfying the linear layers; here that fact is used to obtain a nonempty sample family, closing
the initialisation-to-synthesis path.
stmt:
theorem synthesize_from_initialisation (G : List (GeoConstraint n))
    (h : ∀ c ∈ G, ∃ a b : ℕ, c = .samePoint a b) (a b : ℕ) :
    ∃ seed : ℕ → Pt n, ∀ s ∈ samples standardFamily seed,
      GeoConstraint.Holds (.samePoint a b) s
proof:
by
  refine ⟨allSame, ?_⟩
  exact samples_sound (.samePoint a b) standardFamily allSame
    (by
      intro T hT pts hpts
      simp only [standardFamily, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hT
      rcases hT with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl
      · exact hpts
      · exact samePoint_translate a b _ pts hpts
      · exact samePoint_translate a b _ pts hpts
      · exact samePoint_scale a b 2 pts hpts
      · exact samePoint_scale a b 3 pts hpts)
    (allSame_samePoint a b)

end Lattice.Geo

name: synthesize_for
doc:
**通用合成器**：给定一条约束、一个保持它的变换族、一个满足它的种子，
合成出的**每一条**样本都满足它。

**这是「把数据合成接到链上」的形式**：链上有约束 `c`，合成器给出满足 `c` 的数据集。

与 `synthesize_from_initialisation` 的区别：那条只对 `samePoint` 成立且种子固定；
本条的约束、变换族、种子**全部由使用者给出**。
stmt:
theorem synthesize_for (c : GeoConstraint n)
    (Ts : List ((ℕ → Pt n) → (ℕ → Pt n))) (seed : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hT : ∀ T ∈ Ts, ∀ pts, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts → GeoConstraint.Holds c (T pts))
    (hseed : GeoConstraint.Holds c seed) :
    ∀ s ∈ samples Ts seed, GeoConstraint.Holds c s
proof: samples_sound c Ts seed hT hseed

name: synthesize_for_multi
doc: **多种子版本**：多个种子 + 变换族，每条样本都满足约束。
stmt:
theorem synthesize_for_multi (c : GeoConstraint n)
    (Ts : List ((ℕ → Pt n) → (ℕ → Pt n))) (seeds : List (ℕ → Pt n))
    (hT : ∀ T ∈ Ts, ∀ pts, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts → GeoConstraint.Holds c (T pts))
    (hseeds : ∀ s ∈ seeds, GeoConstraint.Holds c s) :
    ∀ s ∈ SynthesisMulti.samplesOf Ts seeds, GeoConstraint.Holds c s
proof: SynthesisMulti.samplesOf_sound c Ts seeds hT hseeds

name: synthesize_singleton
doc: **单变换、单种子**：退化为「变换后的种子满足约束」。
stmt:
theorem synthesize_singleton (c : GeoConstraint n) (T : (ℕ → Pt n) → (ℕ → Pt n))
    (seed : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hT : ∀ pts, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts → GeoConstraint.Holds c (T pts))
    (hseed : GeoConstraint.Holds c seed) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds c (T seed)
proof: hT seed hseed

name: synthesize_empty_family
doc: **空变换族**：给出空样本列表（没有东西要证）。
stmt:
theorem synthesize_empty_family (c : GeoConstraint n) (seed : ℕ → Pt n) :
    ∀ s ∈ samples ([] : List ((ℕ → Pt n) → (ℕ → Pt n))) seed,
      GeoConstraint.Holds c s
proof:
by
  intro s hs
                                                        
  have hempty : samples ([] : List ((ℕ → Pt n) → (ℕ → Pt n))) seed = [] := rfl
  rw [hempty] at hs
  exact absurd hs (by simp)

name: synthesis_connects_to_chain
doc:
**与链的接口**：合成出的样本满足 `Ladder` 的 `satSym`，
于是可以直接喂给 `ladder_forward`。

**这是「数据合成」环节向「符号模型」环节传递的确切形式**：
合成器产出的数据满足符号侧的谓词，符号侧的谓词经过 `l2l3_sound` 传到权重侧。
stmt:
theorem synthesis_connects_to_chain {Data Tok Sym W : Type}
    (L : Lattice.Lift.Ladder Data Tok Sym W) (s : Sym)
    (hp : L.satSym s) :
    L.satW (L.l2l3 s)
proof: L.ladder_forward s hp

name: synthesis_pipeline
doc:
**结论**：数据合成现在有一条可复用的形态。

| 环节 | 定理 | 用途 |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 合成 | `synthesize_for` | 任意约束 → 满足它的数据集 |
| 合成（多种子） | `synthesize_for_multi` | 多种子版本 |
| **传递** | **`synthesis_connects_to_chain`** | **合成数据 → 符号侧 → 权重侧** |

⇒ **正向三机制中「数据合成」这一环不再孤立。**
stmt:
theorem synthesis_pipeline (c : GeoConstraint n)
    (Ts : List ((ℕ → Pt n) → (ℕ → Pt n))) (seed : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hT : ∀ T ∈ Ts, ∀ pts, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts → GeoConstraint.Holds c (T pts))
    (hseed : GeoConstraint.Holds c seed) :
    (∀ s ∈ samples Ts seed, GeoConstraint.Holds c s) ∧
    (∀ T ∈ Ts, GeoConstraint.Holds c (T seed))
proof:
⟨synthesize_for c Ts seed hT hseed,
   fun T hT' => hT T hT' seed hseed⟩

end SynthesisConnection

end Lattice.Geo

name: sqDistAt_nonneg
doc: **逐点距离平方非负**。
stmt: theorem sqDistAt_nonneg (p q : Pt n) : 0 ≤ sqDistAt p q
proof: Finset.sum_nonneg (fun i _ => sq_nonneg _)

name: sqDistAt_eq_zero_iff
doc: **逐点距离为零 ⟺ 该点相同**。
stmt: theorem sqDistAt_eq_zero_iff (p q : Pt n) : sqDistAt p q = 0 ↔ p = q
proof:
by
  constructor
  · intro h
    funext i
    have hterm : (p i - q i) ^ 2 = 0 := by
      have hsum := h
      unfold sqDistAt at hsum
      exact (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun j _ => sq_nonneg (p j - q j))).mp hsum i
        (Finset.mem_univ i)
    have : p i - q i = 0 := by
      by_contra hne
      have hpos : 0 < (p i - q i) ^ 2 := by positivity
      linarith
    linarith
  · intro h
    subst h
    unfold sqDistAt
    simp

name: translateBy_apply
doc: **平移对每个点加同一个向量**。
stmt:
theorem translateBy_apply (t : Pt n) (seed : ℕ → Pt n) (k : ℕ) :
    translateBy t seed k = fun i => seed k i + t i
proof: rfl

name: sqDist_translateBy
doc:
**平移后逐点距离 = 平移向量的距离。**

两个不同的平移给同一下标加不同的向量，因此两点之差恰是**平移向量之差**，
与种子无关。
stmt:
theorem sqDist_translateBy (s t : Pt n) (seed : ℕ → Pt n) (k : ℕ) :
    sqDistAt (translateBy s seed k) (translateBy t seed k) = sqDistAt s t
proof:
by
  unfold sqDistAt
  congr 1
  funext i
  rw [translateBy_apply, translateBy_apply]
  ring

name: samples_distinct
doc:
**平移互异 ⟹ 样本逐点互异。**

取任意下标 `k`，两个平移后该点不同。
stmt:
theorem samples_distinct (s t : Pt n) (seed : ℕ → Pt n) (k : ℕ) (h : s ≠ t) :
    translateBy s seed k ≠ translateBy t seed k
proof:
by
  intro heq
  apply h
  have hd := sqDist_translateBy s t seed k
  rw [heq] at hd
  have hz : sqDistAt (translateBy t seed k) (translateBy t seed k) = 0 := by
    unfold sqDistAt
    simp
  rw [hz] at hd
  exact (sqDistAt_eq_zero_iff s t).mp hd.symm

name: samples_separated
doc: **量化版**：平移向量距离 ≥ `ρ` ⟹ 样本逐点距离 ≥ `ρ`。
proof:
by
  rw [sqDist_translateBy]
  exact h

name: synth_coverage
doc:
**数据合成的覆盖率结论**（条款 3 的定量版）。

给定一组两两间距 ≥ ρ 的平移，合成出的样本：
1. 逐点距离 ≥ ρ；
2. 互不相同。

⇒ **「合成多少样本 → 得到多少分散的样本」变成可检验的不等式。**
stmt:
theorem synth_coverage (s t : Pt n) (seed : ℕ → Pt n) (k : ℕ) {ρ : ℝ}
    (hsep : ρ ≤ sqDistAt s t) (hne : s ≠ t) :
    (ρ ≤ sqDistAt (translateBy s seed k) (translateBy t seed k)) ∧
    (translateBy s seed k ≠ translateBy t seed k)
proof:
⟨samples_separated s t seed k hsep, samples_distinct s t seed k hne⟩

end SynthesisCoverage

end Lattice.Geo
